definition: A line of cells going across a table.
example: Row 3 contains the club name and its student count.

definition: A line of cells going down a table.
example: Column B contains the student counts.

definition: One box in a spreadsheet where a row and column meet.
example: Cell B3 contains the number of students in the club.

definition: Information arranged in rows and columns.
example: The table puts each club name beside its student count.

definition: A picture that presents data so people can compare or understand it.
example: The chart uses bars to compare the club counts.

definition: Facts or values that can be stored and used.
example: The data shows that twelve students chose chess.

definition: A name or short piece of text that identifies something.
example: The label under each bar names the club.

definition: The information stored in a cell or variable.
example: The value in B3 is 12.

definition: A check of how two things are similar or different.
example: Our comparison shows that chess has more students than art.

definition: A measurement such as length, width or height.
example: Check each dimension of the model against the eraser.

definition: The measurement from one end of an object to the other.
example: The length of the eraser is 50 millimetres.

definition: The measurement from one side of an object to the other.
example: The width of the eraser is 20 millimetres.

definition: The measurement from the bottom of an object to its top.
example: The height of the eraser is 10 millimetres.

definition: A representation used to show what an object is like.
example: The digital model has the same dimensions as the eraser.

definition: Information or a signal given to a computer or program.
example: Pressing button A provides an input to the program.

definition: Information or a signal produced by a computer or program.
example: The displayed number is an output from the counter.

definition: A named place in a program that stores a value which can change.
example: The variable count stores the number of button presses.

definition: A control that you press or select to make something happen.
example: Press the button to add one to the counter.

definition: A value or device used to keep track of how many times something happens.
example: The counter increases by one after each button press.

definition: A check used to find out whether something works as expected.
example: We test the program by pressing the button three times.

definition: Information about work that can help someone improve it.
example: The feedback says to check the displayed total after a reset.

definition: An expression that tells a spreadsheet how to calculate a result.
example: The formula =B2+B3 adds two cell values.

definition: A named operation or group of instructions that performs a task.
example: The function SUM adds a range of spreadsheet values.

definition: The amount found by adding all the relevant values.
example: The total is the number of bottles collected by all teams.

definition: A number found by adding the values and dividing by how many values there are.
example: The average for 10, 20 and 30 is 20.

definition: Instructions that a program repeats.
example: The loop repeats the delivery three times.

definition: The place where an object is located.
example: The sprite starts at position x equals zero.

definition: To return something to its starting state.
example: Click the green flag to reset the sprite and delivery count.

definition: A device that detects or measures something, such as light or distance.
example: A distance sensor measures how far away an object is.

definition: A limit at which a response changes.
example: The threshold is 18 centimetres, so only larger distances trigger the warning.

definition: A test that a program evaluates as true or false.
example: The condition checks whether the distance is greater than 18.

definition: A way to send signals without wires using radio waves.
example: The micro:bit uses radio to send ALERT to the receiver.

definition: Information sent from one person or device to another.
example: The receiver shows an icon when the message is ALERT.

definition: An error that makes a program behave incorrectly.
example: The bug makes the app show the wrong lunch choice.

definition: An action or occurrence that a program can respond to.
example: A button click is an event that starts the instructions.

definition: What happens or is produced after an action or calculation.
example: The result of the test is a message showing the chosen lunch.

definition: A single binary digit, either zero or one.
example: One bit can store either 0 or 1.

definition: A number system that uses only the digits zero and one.
example: The binary number 101 represents five.

definition: The base-ten number system, which uses the digits zero to nine.
example: The decimal number five is written as 101 in binary.

definition: One symbol used to write a number.
example: Each digit in 101 is either zero or one.

definition: The value a digit has because of its position in a number.
example: The leftmost place value in four-bit binary is eight.

definition: A whole number, including zero and negative whole numbers.
example: The integer 4 can be stored in the quantity variable.

definition: A programmable graphic object in Scratch.
example: The Player sprite moves when the arrow key is pressed.

definition: A trick that uses a fake message or website to steal private information.
example: The phishing message asks for the school-account password.

definition: Software made to harm a device, disrupt it or steal information.
example: The unsafe download installs malware on the computer.

definition: Malware that blocks access to files or a device and demands payment.
example: The ransomware locks the project files and demands money.

definition: A secret set of characters used to help prove that someone may access an account.
example: Keep your password private when a message asks you to share it.

definition: An action or safeguard that reduces the chance or harm of a problem.
example: A separate backup provides protection against losing the only project copy.

definition: The possibility that something harmful may happen.
example: Saving only one copy creates a risk of losing the project.

definition: How likely something is to happen.
example: Repeated failed logins increase our concern about the probability of an account attack.

definition: The effect or harm caused by a problem.
example: A separate backup reduces the impact of losing the working file.

definition: Facts or observations that support an explanation or decision.
example: The repeated password requests are evidence that the message is suspicious.

definition: A separate copy kept so that information can be recovered if the working copy is lost.
example: Keep a backup of the project in a separate location.

definition: Something chosen to be dealt with before other things.
example: Protecting the only project copy is our first priority.
